newsitem.title: GERMANY: INSTANT VIEW - Bonn statement on forex markets.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Bonn statement on forex markets.

text.p: The following are economists' comments on the statement released by the German government on the current conditions on the foreign exchange markets, in which it said there was no reason to dramatise the situation.

"There is nothing new in that statement and I would say it is rather disappointing. The expectation had been that they would use much stronger wording than they did. We expect the markets to react to this in the opposite way -- that is by selling the mark and buying the dollar.
NICK PARSONS, CHIEF OF CURRENCY STRATEGY, PARIBAS, LONDON
"Tactically this move is going to backfire and the German authorities are going to regret this."
Parsons said the Bonn government left markets confused today over whether it would make a statement and who would make it.
"If they can't sort out their own public relations you wonder how they are going to sort out the foreign exchange market," he said.

"It's an invitation to sell more marks... this is not just a phenomenon which is driven by dollar strength, this is a period of all-round mark weakness and reflects insecurity about the German economy and EMU," he said.

"The most charitable explanation is that the German authorities were constructing a bear trap (with its statement) but I give that only a five percent probability. I don't think this statement will have the calming effect that was desired."
MATTHIAS HANSMANN, HEAD OF BOND AND CURRENCY RESEARCH, COMMERZBANK, FRANKFURT:
"I don't think we have to fear intervention. The dollar strength is driven by expectations of a large EMU with a soft euro."
Hansmann said that French budget figures due on July 21 may lead to a further appreciation of the dollar.
"If the dollar reaches 1.85 marks or 1.90 marks, those are levels where the central banks can intervene but at the moment at close to 1.80 marks I don't expect intervention."
Hansmann also said the government lost credibility over this statement and due to its back-and-forth over planned tax reforms.
